RRB Photo and Signature Size

Railway Recruitment Board notices for NTPC, Group D, ALP and Technician posts set size ranges for the photo and the signature. Choose the range your notice states and prepare each file.

Size ranges last reviewed: 2026-10-04. Always confirm against your exam notification.

Compression tool

Target size Target size:
Exam range: Targets sit a little below the maximum. Check your notice.
Advanced settings

By default the tool keeps quality reasonable (about 62% or higher) and reduces dimensions to reach small targets; tick “Keep dimensions” to prefer full size at lower quality. Aspect ratio is always preserved and images are never enlarged. PNG is lossless and may not reach a small target; JPEG/WebP are lossy. JPEG replaces transparency with white; WebP and PNG keep it.

What RRB notices ask for

Requirements change with every notification. The ranges on this page are figures commonly reported for recent 2026 notices by exam-preparation websites, and the sources do not always agree. We have not verified them against each official PDF, so always follow the notification or instructions on the official application portal for your exam.

Reports about recent RRB ALP and Technician 2026 notices describe a live photograph captured during the application and a signature uploaded as a JPEG of about 30–49 KB. Other railway notices have been described with different ranges, such as 20–50 KB for a photo or up to 70 KB, so the range depends on the notification. That is why the presets here are named by range.

Choosing the right preset

If your notice says 30 to 49 KB, choose Range 30–49 KB. The target is 46 KB, which leaves room below 49 KB even if the portal counts 1,000 bytes per KB. If your notice says 20 to 50 KB, choose that range instead. For anything else, type the maximum into the custom size box and subtract a few KB.

Signature tips for railway forms

Use a black or dark blue pen on plain white paper, sign inside a clear box, and photograph it in even light. Crop with a small margin. A signature scan often compresses very small, so a minimum such as 30 KB may need a larger, sharper image. The tool shows a warning when the result is under the minimum for the range you picked.

Live photo capture

When a notice says the photograph is captured live, you do not upload a photo file. Follow the on-screen guidance, such as a plain background, good light, no cap or dark glasses, and a face looking straight at the camera. This tool is then only needed for the signature and any other documents.

Other documents

Railway applications may also need certificates or ID uploads with their own limits, sometimes in PDF form. This tool handles images only. If a document is a scanned image of a certificate, compress it to the stated size, and keep the text readable.

Check before you submit

Confirm the format, the file size in the result card, the clarity of your signature, and the file name rules. Keep the original scans. If the portal gives a vague upload error, compare the size in KB and the format against your notice first.

Quick checklist

Check the notification for your post, choose the matching range, aim a few KB below the maximum, stay above the minimum, and keep a clean white background for the signature. If the upload still fails, try another browser, avoid special characters in the file name, and confirm the file extension matches the real format. Keep originals until your application is complete and the confirmation page is saved.

Common questions

Is the RRB signature range always 30–49 KB?

No. It has been reported for some recent notices, but other notices use different ranges. Check yours.

Can I upload a PNG signature?

Notices normally ask for JPEG. Use JPEG output here to get a real .jpg file.
